descriptionChirho: The noun revivim (always plural) denoting 'showers, copious rain,' used poetically for God's blessing through rainfall (Deut 32:2, Jer 3:3, 14:22, Mic 5:6, Ps 65:11, 72:6). All four clusters share this single meteorological referent with variation only in prepositions: bare noun (showers), ke- (like showers), be- (with showers), and waw+ke- (and like droplets). Arabic wabilat/amtar (وَابِلَات/أَمْطَار) 'downpours/rains,' Spanish lluvias/aguaceros 'rains/showers,' Hindi varsha/barish (वर्षा/बारिश) 'rain,' Korean sonagi (소나기) 'shower,' and Swahili mvua/manyunyu 'rain/drizzle' consistently denote precipitation throughout.
